sections.h2: Ways to sell in O'Fallon, Illinois
sections.html:
O'Fallon owners can go with an agent, run the sale themselves, or accept an offer from a company that buys for cash. The right pick turns on the house's condition, the lender's timeline and how much repair work you are willing to manage.

This O'Fallon is in St. Clair County, east of St. Louis, and it is not the O'Fallon in St. Charles County, Missouri, so make sure any records or tax searches use the Illinois city. Population is 32,656, up from 32,289 in 2020. Much of the housing stands in subdivisions built since the 1980s and again after Interstate 64 was widened in the 1990s, with names such as Thornbury Hill, Nolin Creek Estates, Fairwood Hills, Deer Creek and Forest Hills.

  • An agent listing makes sense when the house is ready to occupy and similar sales nearby are easy to find.
  • A sale by owner works when you have the time to show the house and handle paperwork with a title company.
  • A cash purchase works for deferred maintenance, a leased rental, or an inherited property. Get any offer in writing and set it beside a listing price minus commission and repairs.

sections.h2: Scott Air Force Base and buyers on orders
sections.html:
O'Fallon is about 5 miles from Scott Air Force Base and roughly 17 miles from downtown St. Louis, which puts a major employer within a short drive. Many residents work at the base, both military and civil service.

If you deal with a buyer who is moving on orders, expect a firm closing date, and keep repair receipts, appliance manuals and a recent utility history ready so the paperwork moves quickly. Which school district the house is in is the next question such buyers ask. Three districts overlap in O'Fallon: Community Consolidated School District 90, Central School District 104 and O'Fallon Township High School District 203. Print the correct one on your listing sheet.

sections.h2: Is an occupancy permit needed when ownership changes?
sections.html:
Yes. The city requires an occupancy permit when the ownership or occupancy of a home changes and no current permit is on file. A residential permit costs $75 as of May 1, 2025 and stays valid for two years.

The city treats the permit as a property maintenance inspection. After you apply, the schedule runs like this:

  • Call to book the inspection appointment within 7 days of applying.
  • Plan on the inspection taking place inside a month of the application.
  • Any violations must be fixed, and the permit follows within a second 30-day window after that first inspection.
  • Water and electricity must be on during the inspection.

The house may be occupied before the inspection as long as no life safety problems exist. Ameren Illinois and the city's utility billing office ask for the occupancy permit number before they open service. The city offers a seller's and a buyer's "as is" letter, and you should ask your lender whether the permit is a condition of closing.

You can apply online, by mail, through the white drop box in the parking lot, or at Community Development inside City Hall. Paying by card adds a 2.35% convenience fee. Landlords are also pointed to the city's Crime-Free Rental Housing Program.

Fill out the city's start or stop service request form, and call Utility Billing at 618-624-4500 extension 1 if you need help. The office is at 255 S Lincoln Avenue and keeps weekday hours, 7 a.m. to 5:15 p.m.

The city bills water and sewer for most O'Fallon addresses and for most of Fairview Heights. A new account is charged a $50 non-refundable new service fee on its first bill. Sewer charges follow an averaging rule: June, July and August sewer use is billed from the average of the October through April water consumption, with 10,000 gallons assumed for a new residence that has no history. A bill that looks too high can mean a leak, and the city will re-read a meter and run a leak check on request.

sections.h2: When are St. Clair County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Property tax in St. Clair County comes due twice a year, in July and September in recent years, and the Treasurer posts a tax sale for unpaid bills later in the fall. The Treasurer's office opens at half past eight and closes at half past four.

Call the Treasurer for the schedule on your next bill, since posted dates carry a tentative label until they are final. Ask your closing agent how the seller's portion of the year's tax is credited at closing, and pay anything past due before the sale so no lien follows the house.

Owners live in 70.2% of O'Fallon homes, so most buyers are families who will want a clean inspection and a clear occupancy permit.

sections.h2: Step by step for an O'Fallon seller
sections.html:
The city handles most of what a sale needs, so it helps to take things in order.

  1. Decide whether to list, sell it yourself or take a cash offer, and compare what each would put in your pocket after repairs and fees.
  2. Look up whether a current occupancy permit is on file. If not, apply online, by mail, in the white drop box or at Community Development.
  3. Book the inspection within 7 days of applying, make sure the water and electricity are on, and fix any violations the inspector lists.
  4. Submit the start or stop service form to Utility Billing so the water account moves on the closing date.
  5. Call the Treasurer about the tax bill and pay anything past due.

A listing gives you time to find the best price, but the occupancy permit and the inspection apply to a listed sale as much as to a cash sale. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands saves you from a long list of repairs and lets you choose a closing date that works.

Landlords who are selling a rental should also look at the city's Crime-Free Rental Housing Program and tell the buyer where the property stands.

sections.h2: Closing checklist for an O'Fallon seller
sections.html: A few tasks decide how smoothly an O'Fallon sale closes. Apply for the occupancy permit as soon as you have a contract, because the inspection and any repairs take more than a month. Have the water and electricity on for the inspector. Tell Utility Billing the closing date, and ask the Treasurer about the tax bill. A cash buyer who takes the house as is can still need the permit, so ask the buyer who will arrange the inspection.

faqs.q: Do I need an occupancy permit to sell my O'Fallon house?
faqs.a: Usually yes, because the city requires one when ownership changes and no current permit is on file. A residential permit costs $75 and lasts two years, and your lender can tell you if closing depends on it.

faqs.q: How long does the O'Fallon occupancy inspection take to schedule?
faqs.a: Contact the city within 7 days of applying, and the inspection must occur within 30 days of the application. The permit itself follows within another 30 days after the first inspection.

faqs.q: Can a buyer move in before the occupancy inspection is done?
faqs.a: Yes, provided there are no life safety issues. The inspection still has to happen and any violations still have to be corrected.

faqs.q: Which county collects property tax on an O'Fallon house?
faqs.a: St. Clair County. The Treasurer bills in two installments, in July and September in recent years. Call the Treasurer for the next bill's dates.

faqs.q: Is O'Fallon, Illinois the same place as O'Fallon, Missouri?
faqs.a: No. They are separate cities in the same metro area. Illinois's O'Fallon is in St. Clair County, so make sure any records or tax searches use the Illinois city.
